title: Citation health vs. article quality correlation (15 Physics articles)
prompt: Score 15 articles in Category:Physics for article quality via the LiftWing articlequality model, parse their citations (CS1/CS2 templates) with mwparserfromhell, and correlate citation health/verifiability with article quality.

expected_output.description: Per-article quality score, citation count, and a correlation between verifiability and quality.

canaries.name: ORES-compatible nested response envelope
canaries.description: LiftWing articlequality returns {"enwiki": {"scores": {"revid": {"articlequality": {"score": {"prediction": ...}}}}}}. The no-skills variant guessed data['output']['prediction'] and burned ~10 min.
canaries.detection: KeyError or wrong values from a flat response assumption.

canaries.name: CS1/CS2 template catalog
canaries.description: 25+ citation templates; the no-skills variant guessed ~15 from memory.
canaries.detection: Citation counts lower than live counts for known citation-heavy articles.

canaries.name: Redirect exclusion
canaries.description: Category members can be redirects; exclude them (AB: 15 vs 14 articles).

checks.detail: For up to 5 sampled articles, re-score via LiftWing articlequality on the same revision and compare predictions.
checks.pass_condition: Predictions identical (model is deterministic per revision).

checks.detail: Code navigates the nested ORES envelope.
checks.pass_condition: Code contains the 'scores' and 'articlequality' path (or equivalent explicit navigation).

checks.detail: Per-article quality + citation count + a stated correlation.
checks.pass_condition: All fields present; correlation computed from the collected data (not asserted from memory).

port_notes: AB result: the ML response envelope was the single biggest gotcha across all 12 tasks. v1 is deterministic (same revision, same prediction).
